title: Digitalizing Salmonids Farming: The Why, What and How
gist: Pre-tax ROCE at leading Norwegian salmon farmers fell from ~20% (2016) to <10% (2025-early 2026) on cost inflation and capital intensity; a cyclical recovery into 2027-2028 is likely but not structural. BCG argues AI-driven decision making across five domains could add >NOK 6/kg EBIT in 3-5 years, requiring farmers to buy single-source supplier tools but build integrated, business-led decision support.

insights.claim: Pre-tax ROCE for leading Norwegian salmonids farmers fell from about 20% in 2016 to below 10% in 2025 and early 2026, despite salmon prices contributing positively to returns.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Sector-wide return erosion despite price strength signals a structural cost problem; value Norwegian salmon equities on cost trajectory, not price.
insights.quote: Return on capital employed (pre tax ROCE, NOK) for leading Norwegian salmonids farmers has fallen from ~20% in 2016 to <10% during 2025 and early 2026.

insights.claim: Norwegian salmon farming returns compressed over the decade to Q3 2026 because production costs rose rapidly and production became more capital intensive, outweighing positive price achievement.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Monitor cost per kg and capital intensity per harvested kg as the key drivers of farmer ROCE.
insights.quote: returns compressed due to rapidly increasing production cost and increased capital intensity of production
insights.locator: Over the decade through to Q3’26

insights.claim: Salmon farming cost inflation over 10+ years was driven by lower input productivity (e.g. more vessels used per harvested kg), higher supplier raw material costs especially feed via FX and commodity prices, and shifting supplier economics.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Feed commodity prices and NOK FX are key cost-side inputs to track for salmon farmer margins; supplier pricing power is rising.
insights.quote: higher use of e.g. vessels per harvested kg
insights.locator: The high cost inflation in the industry

insights.claim: As of Q4 2026, a return recovery for Norwegian salmon farmers into 2027 and 2028 is likely, as salmon price growth and easing biological and FX headwinds offset feed prices at all-time highs.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Supports a cyclical upturn view on Norwegian salmon farmer earnings through 2028, with feed cost as the main offsetting risk.
insights.quote: a return recovery into 2027 and 2028 is on the cards
insights.locator: As of Q4 2026, a return recovery

insights.claim: The expected salmon farming recovery is driven mostly by historical investments starting to pay off, including post smolt, new vaccines against reemerging challenges, and preventive and proactive sea lice treatments, plus favorable seawater temperatures.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Biological improvements (lice, vaccines, post smolt) are leading indicators for mortality and cost improvements; partly weather-dependent and so not fully durable.
insights.locator: As of Q4 2026, a return recovery

insights.claim: Even if the 2027-2028 salmon return recovery materializes, it will not come from fundamentally reshaped decision making, so without better operating decisions farmers risk another cycle of margin compression.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Treat the upcoming recovery as cyclical rather than structural; avoid extrapolating recovered margins absent operational change.
insights.quote: If the return recovery manifests, it will not be due to farmers fundamentally reshaping decision making processes.

themes.theme: Salmon farming as a digital laggard

insights.claim: Salmonids farming still relies heavily on experience-based decision making; data volume and quality are growing rapidly but rarely analyzed to isolate outcome drivers or used in day-to-day decisions.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Untapped operational data implies upside for farmers that operationalize analytics and for data/AI suppliers to aquaculture.
insights.quote: Salmonids farming remains an industry with a high degree of experience-based decision making.

insights.claim: Salmonids farming lags comparable industries including other protein farming and agriculture on digitalization, where leaders already use it to reshape processing yield, feed selection, and S&OP to improve returns.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Other protein/ag sectors provide a playbook and benchmark for the productivity gains available to salmon farmers.
insights.quote: Salmonids farming lag other comparable industries on digitalization

insights.claim: BCG identifies five digitalization priorities for salmon farmers: S&OP linking harvest, processing, logistics and sales; biomass planning and site outfitting; feeding and selection of roe, vaccines and feed recipes; ROI-based treatment and fish health decisions; and business process automation.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Use as a checklist to assess which salmon farmers are digitalizing the highest-value decisions.
insights.locator: Farmers should structure their digitalization efforts

insights.claim: Together, the five digitalization priorities could add more than NOK 6/kg in EBIT for salmonids farmers within three to five years.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A >NOK 6/kg EBIT uplift is material to farmer margins; a quantifiable upside for operators that execute on AI-driven decisions.
insights.quote: Together, these priorities hold a potential above 6 NOK/kg EBIT improvement for salmonids farmers in the coming 3 to 5 years.
insights.locator: Farmers should structure their digitalization efforts

themes.theme: Buy supplier tools vs build proprietary decision support

insights.claim: Aquaculture tech suppliers are best placed where a single data source answers the question, such as biomass monitoring, start-stop feeding via pellet detection, and preventive sea lice management, and farmers should buy these where ROI is proven.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Single-data-source point solutions (biomass, feeding cameras, lice) are the commercial sweet spot for aquaculture tech vendors.
insights.quote: Here, farmers should buy what they see ROI on.

insights.claim: The highest-impact salmon farming decisions are complex and multidisciplinary, requiring data from multiple suppliers simultaneously, so farmers must orchestrate or build decision support and automation themselves rather than rely on vendors.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Limits the addressable market of single-point aquaculture vendors; favors farmers with internal data/AI capabilities and integration layers.
insights.quote: delivering value from digitalization comes down to improved decision making and not improved access to data

insights.claim: AI is dramatically cutting the cost of building proprietary software, turning months-long prototypes into weeks and removing the historical bottleneck of bespoke software for niche industries like salmon farming.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: AI-enabled in-house builds lower barriers in niche verticals and may compress demand for bespoke vertical software vendors.
insights.quote: prototypes that used to take months now take weeks
insights.locator: Historically, the cost for developing industry-bespoke software

insights.claim: The AI-enabled build-plus-buy paradigm favors larger salmon farmers with scale, though mid-market operators still have a path to catch up.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Scale advantage in digitalization may widen performance gaps between large and mid-sized farmers, supporting consolidation.
insights.quote: This paradigm favors larger companies with scale, but mid-market operators still have a path to catch up.
insights.locator: Historically, the cost for developing industry-bespoke software

themes.theme: AI transformation is 70% people and process

insights.claim: BCG's experience is that 70% of AI transformation success comes from navigating people, organization and process, about 20% from data and technology, and 10% from algorithms, so technology is no longer the bottleneck.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Judge AI adoption by organizational change and P&L-owner accountability, not tech spend or model choice.
insights.quote: Technology is therefore no longer the bottleneck.
insights.locator: Technology is therefore no longer the bottleneck

insights.claim: BCG advises farmers to pick a few big bets on high-value value-chain decisions rather than working incrementally through many small pilots, with P&L owners leading and accountable and IT enabling but not owning.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Pilot-heavy AI programs are a red flag; concentrated, business-led bets signal likelier value capture.
insights.quote: Don’t work incrementally through several pilots of smaller use cases
insights.locator: To get going today, farmers should

insights.claim: Farmers should build a common context layer pooling data from all suppliers for reuse across internal use cases, and design builds for how processes will run 2-3 years out to avoid technology debt.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A shared cross-vendor data layer is the strategic asset; vendors that resist data interoperability may lose share.
insights.quote: Establish a common context layer leveraging all available data from all suppliers that all internally built use cases can reuse
